channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee extends its downfall due to surging US Treasury Yields
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends its previous week’s downfall against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with the USD/INR rising above 95.90. The pair declined a little over 1% last week due to rising United States (US) Treasury Yields and elevated oil prices.

item.title: Gold bears retain control as markets brace for Fed rate hike
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains on the defensive on Tuesday as a stronger US Dollar (USD), rising US Treasury yields and US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike expectations create a challenging backdrop for the non-yielding metal.

item.title: Copper: AI slowdown fears pressure prices – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that Copper is retreating as calls from major technology executives to slow AI development hit tech stocks and dampen expectations for data-centre investment.

item.title: Experts agree: Fed will follow monetary tightening path even beyond September meeting
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) outperforms its major currency peers on Tuesday, following strong United States (US) Treasury Yields on expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will remain on the monetary tightening path even after hiking interest rates at the policy meeting on Wednesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Two-way risks into BoJ meeting – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong notes USD/JPY has rebounded as higher UST yields, a firmer USD and rising Oil offset support from Bank of Japan (BoJ) tightening expectations. He warns against extrapolating gains ahead of Friday’s BoJ meeting, with markets almost fully pricing another hike.

item.title: Swiss Franc struggles near lows as monetary policy divergence boosts US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) consolidates losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with the USD/CHF trading just below one-and-a-half-month highs at the 0.8200 level.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Looking for 0.7100 break against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: Quek Ser Leang at UOB notes AUD/USD fell more sharply than anticipated to 0.7109, leaving short-term conditions oversold and favouring consolidation between 0.7110 and 0.7155 intraday.

item.title: British Pound trades mixed after steady UK employment report, CPI data eyed
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) reflects a mixed performance against its currency peers after the release of the United Kingdom (UK) labor market data for three months ending July.

item.title: Bank of Japan: Gradual normalisation path outlined – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Chong Hoon Park and Nicholas Chia expect the Bank of Japan to hike its policy rate by 25bps to 1.25% at the 17-18 September meeting.

item.title: Bank Of England: Jobs data supports steady policy – ING
item.description: ING economist James Smith argues that recent United Kingdom (UK) jobs data underline a cooler labour market and weaker wage dynamics, reducing the risk of another inflation surge.

item.title: Euro remains depressed as Eurozone sentiment and trade data fail to inspire
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains on the defensive against the US Dollar (USD) as investors brace for the first interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed) after three years.

item.title: Euro: Downside pressure targets 1.1490 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang highlights renewed EUR/USD weakness after a sharper-than-expected drop below 1.1565 to 1.1522. He sees scope for a further test of 1.1520 intraday, with 1.1490 as the next key support over the coming weeks.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $62.82 per troy ounce, down 0.68% from the $63.25 it cost on Monday.

item.title: Brent: Higher risk premium and retest of highs – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Energy Strategists Joe DeLaura and Florence Schmit revise their Brent outlook higher as Middle East disruptions tighten supply routes.

item.title: Germany ZEW sentiment edges higher but misses expectations
item.description: Germany’s ZEW Survey Economic Sentiment rose slightly to 34.7 in September from 34.2 in August, although the reading falls short of market expectations of 37.

item.title: US Dollar: Consolidation with two-way risks – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong notes the US Dollar Index (DXY) around 99.5, supported by higher Oil, elevated UST yields and softer risk sentiment. He highlights tentative bullish daily momentum and two-way risks, with resistance near 99.80–100.30 and support around 99.30–98.00.

item.title: WTI clings to gains near mid-$99.00s, eyes multi-month top amid supply concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – catches fresh bids following the previous day's two-way price swings and sticks to its strong intraday gains through the first half of the European session on Tuesday.

item.title: British Pound: Stronger growth offsets labour weakness – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman says the Pound is holding up better than expected despite the worsening energy price shock.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds gains as higher oil prices weigh on Japanese Yen
item.description: AUD/JPY gains ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 110.40 during European hours on Tuesday. The currency cross appreciates as the Japanese Yen (JPY) faces headwinds from rising global oil prices, which significantly inflate import costs for Japan's energy-dependent economy.

item.title: CEE FX: Higher rates seen cushioning currencies – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky explains that a surge in energy prices, a jump in US 10-year yields to 5% and a stronger Dollar have hit CEE currencies and pushed local rates higher.

item.title: Canadian Dollar languishes near 0.8200 as Fed tightening bets buoy US Dollar
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) hovers near monthly lows against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, as rising expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will tighten its monetary policy on Wednesday underpin speculative demand for the Greenback.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Rate hiking path and global yields – BNY
item.description: BNY’s John Velis expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25bp at this week’s FOMC meeting and sees another hike as likely later this year.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Finds bids below 61.8% Fibo retracement
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) recovers half of its early losses against the US Dollar (USD), but is still 0.17% down at around 0.5770 during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro advances against Japanese Yen ahead of ZEW Survey data
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its gains for the second consecutive day, trading around 179.00 during European hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold struggles near multi‑week low as Fed hike bets and geopolitical risks boost USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) drifts lower for the second straight day – also marking the third day of a negative move – and trades around the $4,265-$4,264 region, down 0.80% during the first half of the European session on Tuesday.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Funding role versus haven status – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses whether the Swiss Franc (CHF) will shift from safe haven to funding currency status. Foley highlights Swiss National Bank (SNB) intervention during the Iran war, subdued Swiss inflation, and a zero policy rate.

item.title: Australian Dollar hangs near three-week low, above 0.7100 as USD stands firm ahead of Fed
item.description: The AUD/USD pair sticks to a negative bias for the second consecutive day and trades around the 0.7120 region during the early part of the European session on Tuesday.

item.title: Dow Jones futures fall as traders brace for Fed rate decision
item.description: Dow Jones futures fall by 0.56% to trade near 52,150 during European hours on Tuesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures decline by 0.42% to trade around 7,590, while Nasdaq 100 futures drop by 0.37% to trade near 29,050.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI seen starting mini hiking cycle - Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kunal Kundu expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to respond to India’s broadening inflation pressures with a new mini rate-hike cycle. Kundu projects a 25bp hike in October, followed by two similar moves in December and February.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Resistance at 155.20 likely to test bulls
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is showing a moderately softer tone against the US Dollar (USD) this week, with all eyes on the monetary policy decisions bu¡y the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Japan (BoJ), due later this week.
